text:
incident-bot: ALARM — Elevated GPU error rate: us-east-1 + us-west-2. Correctable ECC and link resets. Capacity impacted: ~23% of serving GPUs unavailable. Affected instance types: p4d / a100. Jobs returning device errors, retries spiking. https://redwood.monitor/alerts/9876

chad (oncall): seeing a surge of 502s & backend restarts, autoscaler started draining nodes. Noticed many 'device reset' logs in pod stdout.

maria (SRE): i'm on the pager. can someone paste a quick `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu -o wide`? want to see which nodes are NotReady.

nisha (infra): pasted below - most NotReady are in us-east-1-gpu-pool-2
```
NAME                     STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-42              NotReady   node     24d   v1.27.3
gpu-node-43              NotReady   node     12d   v1.27.3
gpu-node-88              Ready      node     2d    v1.27.3
```
We see elevated `gpu.error.corrected` counters and NVLink timeout entries in dmesg.

leo (runtime): on model side we saw KV cache invalidations when clients hit those nodes — causes token latency spikes and retries. stack traces show PCIe bus reset, not consistent with driver panic.

chad (oncall): can we cordon/drain the two NotReady nodes to avoid scheduling? `kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

infra-ci-bot: job/cordon-gpu-nodes started for [gpu-node-42, gpu-node-43]

nisha (infra): draining now. Also pulling 40 replacement instances from spare pool in us-east-1; provisioning ETA 25-40m.

maria (SRE): temporary mitigation: reroute latency-sensitive traffic to eu-west-1 and increase retry backoff. Updating routing policy now.

leo (runtime): diag from one affected host (excerpt):
```
[  +0.123456] nvidia 0000:af:00.0: Corrected ECC error on GPU0
[  +0.000123] PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer, id=00
[  +0.002345] GPU reset due to link recovery
```
Suggests flaky hardware/PCIe fabric. Vendor recommends kernel `5.19` fixes for corner-case link recovery — need patching plan.

chad (oncall): timeline? if replacements take 40m-1h, what's expected capacity recovery and impact to SLA?

nisha (infra): capacity should recover to ~90% after node provisioning and rejoin. We'll monitor for recurrence. cross-region egress will spike while rerouting traffic.

maria (SRE): opening incident review ticket: INC-2026-134. If this is >4h I'll start a postmortem. Issue: fleet-wide corrected ECC increases + sporadic NVLink/PCIe resets leading to node drains.

chad (oncall): FYI cost team: tagging incident for potential overage because of multi-region failover and spare pool usage. @finance

nisha (infra): follow-ups: (1) disable automatic node replacement until we confirm root cause, (2) create metric alert for `gpu.error.corrected` rate per-node, (3) schedule vendor kernel update + PCIe firmware check.

leo (runtime): also add a playback eval to catch degraded output quality when nodes are in mid-reset; noticed client-visible retries causing duplicate completions.

maria (SRE): agreed. i'll add runbook steps for manual PCIe reset via `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <id>` and how to safely drain nodes during replacement.

chad (oncall): thanks everyone. we'll reconvene in #incidents for updates. please post short updates here as things change :thumbsup:
